codeReview.summary: PovServlet implementation is clean, well-structured, and fully covers the feature requirements. The servlet properly handles GET /povs (list with table/empty state), GET /povs?action=new (create form with 6-status dropdown defaulting to PLANNED), and POST /povs (create with server-side validation and PRG redirect). JSP pages use <c:out> for all user-controlled output. Status badges have distinct CSS classes with appropriate visual differentiation (green for COMPLETED/WON, red for LOST, amber for IN_PROGRESS, indigo for PLANNED, gray for CANCELLED). Validation covers all required fields, date parsing, and target-end-date >= start-date constraint. 41 comprehensive integration tests cover happy paths, validation errors, XSS protection, and edge cases. The implementation follows existing project patterns (TimeEntryServlet structure, PRG pattern, error preservation, JDBC DAOs).

issues.description: The status badge rendering uses a verbose <c:choose>/<c:when> chain with 6 branches for each status value. While correct and functional, this could be simplified using PovServlet.getBadgeClass() and getStatusDisplayName() static methods that already exist in the servlet (e.g., via a JSP scriptlet or EL function). However, the current approach is explicit and readable, so this is purely a code style observation.

The <form> tag is opened inside a <c:choose>/<c:when> block but closed outside it. While this works in practice (JSP compiles the combined output), it creates an unclosed tag within each branch. An alternative pattern would use a single <form> tag with a dynamic action attribute. This is a minor readability/maintainability concern, not a functional bug.
